Seminar Title:

Study of role of sterile neutrinos in lepton number violating processes in low and high energy regime

Seminar Type:

Synopsis Seminar

Department:

Physics and Astronomy

Speaker Name:

Debashree Priyadarsini Das ( Rollno : 519ph1006)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Conference Hall, Department of Physics and Astronomy

Date and Time:

30 Apr 2026 11 am

Contact:

Sasmita Mishra

Abstract:

Even though the Standard Model (SM) has been remarkably successful, it still cannot explain some key phenomena such as neutrino masses, dark matter (DM), and the baryon asymmetry of the Universe. In this work, we consider sterile neutrinos as a minimal extension of the SM, capable of providing a unified framework for these phenomena, motivated by their connection to lepton number violation (LNV). We study two well-motivated LNV probes: neutrinoless double beta decay ($0\nu\beta\beta$) and two-sector leptogenesis. We begin by studying $0\nu\beta\beta$ in a framework with three sterile neutrinos, where both active and sterile states can mediate the decay. To capture the effects of the extended neutrino sector, we employ a $6\times6$ unitary parametrization that includes the additional active&ndashsterile mixing angles and $CP$-violating phases. Imposing the exact seesaw relation allows us to express the sterile neutrino masses in terms of the mixing angles, $CP$-violating phases, and lightest mass state of active neutrino, thereby defining the relevant parameter space for evaluating the effective mass $m_{ee}$. Exploring this parameter space, we find that $m_{ee}$ spans from $\mathcal{O}(10^{-4})$ up to the current experimental limits, with sterile neutrino contributions arising across the keV&ndashTeV mass range. Importantly, the obtained results are consistent with existing bounds from charged lepton flavour violation processes and constraints on non-unitarity. We then extend this analysis to a $\chi$EFT framework, where the presence of keV-scale sterile neutrinos significantly alters the predictions by removing the cancellation region in the normal hierarchy and distorting the band in the inverted hierarchy. Finally, we turn to the high-energy regime, where the out-of-equilibrium decays of sterile neutrinos generate the observed baryon asymmetry through two-sector leptogenesis. This is realized in a framework that includes an inert Higgs doublet (IHD) and a dark sector. Although the IHD can act as a WIMP-like DM candidate in the $(80\text{&ndash}500)$ GeV range, its contribution to the relic density is subdominant, which motivates us to focus on this region. In this setup, we find that for the lightest sterile neutrino mass around $10^{10}$ GeV, successful leptogenesis can be achieved, while the observed ratio $\Omega_{\rm DM}/\Omega_{\rm B}\sim 5$ is simultaneously reproduced for GeV-scale dark sector DM candidates.
